drafted_from: tool:read-what-is-on-screen row in tool-rows.json, do-work/read-what-is-on-screen.mjs, do-work/read.swift, read-data/rules.json and test/read-what-is-on-screen.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Watch what I am doing on my Mac for 20 seconds, re-reading the same window every 30 seconds, and tell me which apps and windows I used." It runs tool:read-what-is-on-screen on your Mac and answers one capture per read, as text, never a screenshot.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads the front window's accessibility text for a short watch and answers captures, keeping nothing.
instructions: 1. Turn on Accessibility for the app that runs the tool in System Settings, Privacy & Security; without it the answer is needs_access and nothing is read.

2. Say "Watch my screen for N seconds"; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:read-what-is-on-screen and input {watch_seconds (5 to 240, default 50), tick_seconds (10 to 600, default 60)}.

3. Read the answer: captures, each with at, app, bundle_id, window, url (browsers), reason (changed or tick), and text on a window's first capture in the run or added and removed lines on later ones; a value outside the bounds is refused with the bounds.

4. Know what it never reads: password managers, Keychain, Settings, private browser windows and pages whose address holds a never-read word; passwords, keys and card numbers are replaced with [removed] on your Mac before anything is returned.

worked_examples.title: A 20 second watch while a notes window changes
worked_examples.ask: Watch what I am doing on my Mac for 20 seconds and tell me which windows I used.
worked_examples.given: Read from do-work/read-what-is-on-screen.mjs and do-work/read.swift (a live window read needs the Accessibility grant, so no test runs it; the made-up desktop is worked out from the code): the tool runs `swift read.swift --rules read-data/rules.json --watch-seconds 20 --tick-seconds 30`; Accessibility is on, a Notes window titled "Tuesday meeting" is in front and its text gains one line during the watch.
worked_examples.hands_back: {captures: [{at: <time of the read>, app: "Notes", bundle_id: "com.apple.Notes", window: "Tuesday meeting", reason: "changed", text: "Agenda\nBudget summary"}, {at: <a later time>, app: "Notes", bundle_id: "com.apple.Notes", window: "Tuesday meeting", reason: "tick", added: ["Next steps"], removed: []}]}: the first capture of a window carries its whole text, later ones only the lines added and removed.

worked_examples.title: Accessibility is off
worked_examples.given: From tools/read-what-is-on-screen/test/read-what-is-on-screen.test.mjs and read-data/rules.json: the app that runs the tool has not been given Accessibility.
worked_examples.hands_back: {needs_access: "accessibility", said: "Turn on Accessibility for the app that runs this tool in System Settings, Privacy & Security, so it can read what is on your screen."} and nothing is read.
